key_insight: Physics-informed circuits, compact gauge-field encodings, and operator truncation advance resource-efficient quantum simulation of interacting-field dynamics.
engineering_relevance: These methods reduce qubit and circuit-depth demands on a path toward real-time QCD simulations beyond classical reach.
method: Prepare interacting ground states and simulate heavy-quark energy loss in 1+1D SU(2) lattice gauge theory.
Digitize a fully gauge-fixed SU(2) Hamiltonian in a mixed basis.
Apply Sequency Hierarchy Truncation (SeqHT) to reduce ground-state preparation depth.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantum-hardware validation against classical benchmarks, low-energy observables reproduced to 10⁻³ precision with three qubits per plaquette, and approximately 30% circuit-depth reduction with SeqHT.
watch_item: Larger systems remain resource-limited, and truncations must preserve the observables relevant to each simulation.
paper_title: Digital Quantum Simulation of Dynamics in Interacting Fields
